title: Two-Point Chowla and the Finite-Prefix Indeterminacy of the Liouville Correlation
summary: Two-point Chowla, sum lambda(n)lambda(n+2) = o(x), is open; this folder fixes its status. Proved in Lean: the trivial bound |corr(h,N)| <= N and the witness corr(0,N)=N, so o(N) is not formal; the finite-prefix indeterminacy theorem (negating lambda at one index leaves every shorter prefix identical while the functions differ), l^2-mass 4; and the shifted product's non-multiplicativity, so no Euler product. Numerics (30/30, sieve to 10^9) prove nothing about the limit; the independent check gives 25/26, the one non-pass being S(10^7): 1244 -> 1246. Edition: same theorem as publish/014, the fuller package; no priority claimed.
recipe_md:
Commands are relative to `research/publish/007-two-point-chowla`. Lean 4 v4.35.0-rc2 with Mathlib for the Lean check; numpy and mpmath for the Python checks.

```sh
./check.sh --all          # expect [check] OK Rh46/Chowla.lean and [check] OK Rh46.lean; exit 0
                          # (four non-fatal linter warnings; archived 23 s + 9 s, packaging run 41 s + 57 s)
python3 chowla_two_point.py   # 4-9 min; expect "30 checks pass, 0 fail", exit 0; S(10^7)=1246,
                              # S(10^8)=4632, S(10^9)=43790, alpha = 0.5200 +/- 0.0249, final
                              # line "STATUS OF (STAR): OPEN". Writes verify/chowla_two_point.log.
python3 independent_check.py  # 1-2 min; expect "FINAL: 25/26 checks pass" and exit 1 BY DESIGN;
                              # the single [FAIL] is S2.crosscheck, the recorded 1244 -> 1246 correction.
```

What the numerics can and cannot do, in the scripts' own words: no finite computation can PROVE o(x); a finite computation CAN REFUTE it, and no such x occurs here.
